title: No display / black screen
summary: Works from the cheapest checks through to graphics card and memory faults, in the order that saves the most time.

state.question: What state is the computer in when there is no display?
state.help: No power at all and no display but running fans are completely different problems.

options.label: No power: no lights, no fans
Fans and lights work, but the screen is black
Monitor says no signal but the PC is clearly on
It works when I boot, then goes black later

cable_test.question: Have you tried a different video cable and a different port on the monitor?
cable_test.help: This is free and rules out the single most common cause of a black screen.

options.label: No, same cable and port as always
Yes, tried different cables and ports

output_source.question: Does the monitor have more than one input, and have you selected the right one using its own menu?
output_source.help: Monitors do not detect inputs automatically on many models. Use the buttons on the monitor to select HDMI, DisplayPort or VGA.

options.label: I have not checked the monitor's input menu
The correct input is selected and it still says no signal

gpu_present.question: Does this computer have a separate graphics card?
gpu_present.help: Most desktops with a dedicated GPU also have video output on the motherboard, which lets you test without the card.

options.label: Yes, it has a graphics card and the motherboard also has video output

integrated_no_gpu.question: Is this a laptop, and does pressing the brightness keys make anything appear on the internal screen?
integrated_no_gpu.help: Some laptops send video to the external output only, or apply a backlight that needs cycling.

options.label: It is a laptop and nothing happens with the brightness keys
It is a laptop, and something appeared after cycling brightness or display output
It is a desktop without a separate graphics card

external_monitor_test.question: Does an external monitor connected to the laptop show anything, including a login screen?
external_monitor_test.help: If the external display works, the panel, its cable or its backlight is the problem rather than the graphics hardware.

options.label: No, the external monitor is black too

black_after_boot.question: Does it show the Windows logo and spinner, then go black?
black_after_boot.help: That pattern points at the graphics driver rather than hardware, because Windows has already started.

options.label: Yes, it gets as far as the Windows logo then goes black
It goes black without showing the Windows logo
It goes black after signing in, when the desktop loads

result_power_supply.title: Start with power
result_power_supply.diagnosis: No lights and no fans at all means the power supply, its cable or the wall socket, not the display.
steps: Test the wall socket with a lamp or phone charger, since a dead outlet looks exactly like a dead PC
Check the PSU power switch at the back is set to I, and the cable is clicked in fully at both ends
Disconnect all drives and expansion cards except the motherboard, then retry
Test with a single RAM stick, since a machine with no usable memory often shows nothing
Try a known-good power supply of the same wattage and form factor
Confirm the CPU fan spins at all when the power switch is flicked on
warnings: Never open a power supply. The capacitors inside hold a lethal charge even when unplugged.
Do not use a power supply from another PC unless the wattage and connectors match exactly.

result_cable_first.title: Change the cable before anything else
result_cable_first.diagnosis: A damaged cable or wrong input selection produces a black screen identical to a dead graphics card.
steps: Swap the video cable for a known-good one of the same type
Try a different port on the monitor and select it in the monitor's own input menu
Test the monitor with another device, such as a laptop, to confirm the panel works
On a desktop with a graphics card, confirm the cable is plugged into the card, not the motherboard
Clean the connectors gently and check for bent pins, which cause exactly this symptom
Only after cables, ports and monitors are ruled out should you suspect the graphics hardware
warnings: Do not assume the graphics card has failed until the cable and monitor are ruled out.

result_monitor_input.title: Select the correct input on the monitor
result_monitor_input.diagnosis: Many monitors do not detect an input automatically, and simply show a black screen instead.
steps: Press the buttons or joystick on the monitor to open its own menu
Find Input Source or Source and select the port matching your cable, such as HDMI 1
If unsure, plug the cable into the only port that works with no selection needed, often HDMI 1
Confirm the monitor's own LED shows a normal, not standby, state
Check the power cable to the monitor is fully connected and the monitor input is right
Try a different cable if the screen still says no signal

result_display_switch.title: Windows is using the wrong display
result_display_switch.diagnosis: Pressing the brightness or display-switch keys fixes it, so the machine and graphics hardware are fine.
steps: Use Win plus P to open the projection menu and choose the display you want
Choose PC screen only if you only use the laptop panel, or Duplicate if you want both
If the display menu does not appear, try the hardware keys: Fn plus F7, F8, F9 or F10 vary by laptop
Open Settings > System > Display > Display resolution and set it to Recommended
Check Settings > System > Display > Use dynamic brightness, which can black out very bright panels
Update the graphics driver if this happens regularly after waking
warnings: Do not change the resolution to something custom if the recommended setting looks wrong; that usually means a driver problem.

result_internal_display.title: The internal laptop screen is at fault
result_internal_display.diagnosis: The external display working proves the graphics hardware is fine, so the panel, cable or backlight has failed.
steps: Connect an external monitor and use it with Win plus P set to Duplicate or Extend
Increase the internal panel brightness with the brightness keys to check for a backlight that is alive but dim
Update the graphics driver and the display's own driver through Windows Update
On a laptop, check the panel cable is seated, which requires opening the case or a repair centre
Look closely at the screen with a torch, since a faint image under direct light means the backlight has failed rather than the panel
Consider a repair centre for panel or backlight replacement, which is usually cheaper than a new laptop
warnings: Opening a laptop to reach the screen cable risks damaging the display. If you are not comfortable, use a repair centre.
A laptop with a black screen and faint image under a torch almost always needs a backlight or cable repair rather than a new motherboard.

result_test_integrated.title: Test without the graphics card
result_test_integrated.diagnosis: Moving the cable to the motherboard's video output tells you immediately whether the graphics card is the problem.
steps: Power off and switch the PSU off, then move the monitor cable to the motherboard's HDMI or DisplayPort
If the display works, the graphics card, its power cables or its slot is at fault, so reseat the card and every power connector on it
If there is still no display, reseat the RAM and test one stick at a time, since memory faults produce no video
On a desktop, try the card in a different PCIe slot if the board has a second one
Once you get a display, install the GPU driver with a clean uninstall using DDU
If the card fails in another PC or another slot, the card itself has failed
warnings: Never force a graphics card into a slot. If it does not seat easily with the latch open, something is misaligned and forcing it can damage the slot.
A GPU needs two or three 8-pin power connectors on most models. Missing power causes no display or random shutdowns.

result_ram_then_boot.title: Test memory, then repair the boot
result_ram_then_boot.diagnosis: Fans on, no display, no separate GPU: memory is the first thing to test, then the boot files.
steps: Reseat all RAM, then test with a single stick in the slot closest to the CPU
Run MemTest86 for two full passes with that stick
If memory is clean, boot from Windows install media and choose Repair > Command Prompt
Run bootrec /fixmbr, bootrec /fixboot and bootrec /rebuildbcd
Run chkdsk C: /f /r /x to repair the filesystem
Check the drive's SMART health, since a failing drive cannot hold repaired boot files
warnings: Create a Windows install USB on another working PC first, so you always have boot media available.

result_safe_mode_driver.title: Start in Safe Mode and fix the driver
result_safe_mode_driver.diagnosis: Getting to the Windows logo and spinner means Windows has started, so the fault is almost always a driver.
steps: Interrupt the boot three times, choosing Start your PC in Safe mode when prompted, or hold Shift while clicking Restart
Once in Safe Mode, open Device Manager and expand Display adapters
Right-click the graphics adapter and choose Uninstall device, ticking Delete the driver software
Restart, let Windows install the basic display driver, then install the newest official driver
For a stubborn fault, clean install in Safe Mode using our DDU guide
Update chipset drivers too, since they underpin the graphics driver
Disable Windows Update driver replacement so your working driver is not swapped out again
warnings: After removing the GPU driver you will be on a low-performance basic driver until you install the real one. Have the installer ready.
Do not install third-party driver packages or driver updater tools, which often install unsigned drivers and cause more problems than they solve.
